breath.sama-vritti.name: Sama Vritti
breath.sama-vritti.subtitle: Equal breathing
breath.sama-vritti.what: Breathing in and out for the same count. Sama vritti is Sanskrit for "equal movement". Many people find the steady rhythm settling.
steps: Sit comfortably with your back upright but not stiff, or lie down.
Breathe in through your nose for a count of 4.
Breathe out through your nose for a count of 4.
Keep the breath smooth and quiet, with no pause and no holding.
If 4 feels long, breathe more softly or at your own pace.
skipIf: Your nose is blocked. Breathe gently through your mouth, or choose a meditation today.

breath.deergha.name: Deergha Pranayama
breath.deergha.subtitle: Three-part breath
breath.deergha.what: A slow, full breath that fills the belly, then the ribs, then the upper chest, and empties in the same easy way. Deergha means "long". Here the out-breath is a little longer than the in-breath.
steps: Sit or lie down and rest one hand on your belly and one on your chest.
Breathe in through your nose for 4: let the belly rise, then the ribs widen, then the chest lift a little.
Breathe out through your nose for 6, letting the chest, the ribs and then the belly soften.
Keep it easy. The breath should never feel forced.
If the counts feel long, take smaller breaths at the same pace.
skipIf: You have had surgery on your belly or chest recently.

breath.nadi-shodhana.name: Nadi Shodhana
breath.nadi-shodhana.subtitle: Alternate-nostril breathing
breath.nadi-shodhana.what: Breathing in through one nostril and out through the other, then the other way round. It is also called Anulom Vilom. This beginner version has no breath-holding.
steps: Sit upright and rest your left hand on your knee.
Use your right thumb to close the right nostril and your ring finger to close the left.
Close the right nostril and breathe in through the left for 4. Close the left, open the right, and breathe out for 4.
Breathe in through the right for 4. Close it, open the left, and breathe out for 4. That is one round.
Press lightly. If your arm tires, lower it and breathe normally for a moment.
skipIf: Your nose is blocked or you have a cold.

breath.bhramari.name: Bhramari
breath.bhramari.subtitle: Humming-bee breath
breath.bhramari.what: A slow breath out with a soft, steady hum, like a bee. Bhramara is Sanskrit for a black bee. The sound can be as quiet as you like.
steps: Sit comfortably and close your eyes if you like.
Breathe in slowly through your nose for 4.
With your lips closed, breathe out for 6 while making a soft "mmm" hum.
If you like, rest your index fingers lightly on the small flap at the front of each ear. Never press hard.
Let the hum fade naturally. Take a normal breath whenever you need one.
skipIf: You have an ear or nose infection.

med.breath-awareness.title: Breath awareness
guidance: Sit in a way that lets you stay still and alert: on a chair, a cushion or the floor. Rest your hands. Close your eyes, or lower your gaze.
Let the breath move on its own. You don't need to change it.
Notice where you feel it most clearly: the cool air at the nostrils, or the rise and fall of the belly. Rest your attention there.
Your mind will wander. That is normal. When you notice it has wandered, come back gently to the next breath. Coming back is the practice.
If it helps, count each out-breath from 1 to 10, then start again at 1.
med.breath-awareness.repetitionVariant: If you prefer, silently repeat a word or name you hold dear with each breath. Some people use "so" on the in-breath and "ham" on the out-breath (so'ham, an old Sanskrit phrase often read as "I am that"). Any word that matters to you is fine.
cues: If your mind has wandered, come back to the breath.
Still here. Just the next breath.
Nearly done. Stay with the breath.
med.breath-awareness.closing: When the bell sounds, take one fuller breath. Open your eyes slowly and notice how you feel.
med.breath-awareness.note: Meditation can sometimes bring up strong feelings or memories. You can open your eyes, move or stop at any time.

med.body-scan.title: Body scan
guidance: Sit or lie down comfortably. Close your eyes if you like.
Take two slow breaths, letting each out-breath be a little longer.
Bring your attention to your feet. Notice whatever is there: warmth, pressure, tingling, or nothing much. There is nothing to fix.
Slowly move your attention up through the ankles, calves, knees and thighs, then the hips, lower back, belly, chest and upper back.
Notice your hands, arms and shoulders. Let the shoulders drop a little.
Move to the neck, jaw, face and the top of the head. Soften the jaw and the space between the eyebrows.
Finally, feel the whole body at once, breathing. If you find tension, you don't need to make it go. Notice it, and keep moving.
med.body-scan.closing: When the bell sounds, move your fingers and toes. Open your eyes slowly.
med.body-scan.note: Meditation can sometimes bring up strong feelings or memories. You can open your eyes, move or stop at any time.
